races.name: Squadron Flyer At Aldwark Manor Estate Ebf Restricted Maiden Stakes (for Horses In Bands C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Harrogate Theatre Panto Tickets Now On-sale Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Masterly
runners_data.note: A lightly raced five-year-old last seen 1077 days ago, making his record almost impossible to assess; Charlie Johnston's patient handling may have him ready to peak fresh but the lengthy absence and single form entry (3rd on Soft over 9f) leave his stamina for 1m3f and current condition deeply uncertain.

runners_data.name: Time Thief
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good last time out and brings a profile tailor-made for this trip and surface — David Egan keeps him prominent tracking Why Not Me, and his 1/1 record on similar going makes him the most form-reliable runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's mare holds a course-and-distance profile on her best form (2nd over 11f Soft, 4th over 14f Good) and Jason Hart's patient hold-up style suits a race likely run at a steady tempo; she will need to produce more than her recent 4-4-2 sequence suggests.

runners_data.name: Why Not Me
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Stuart Williams who will dictate on the Good ground, but the [STYLE_FIT] tag signals a horse racing outside its most comfortable pattern — its best form is over shorter distances on Standard, and leading for 1m3f on Good represents a test of both stamina and adaptability; Oisin Murphy's class helps, but discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Feelin' Free
runners_data.note: Jack Jones's three-year-old has winning form over 10f on Soft and showed pace when second last time, but as a genuine prominent type forced into a midfield position by the field's makeup, it faces the challenge of racing in a manner that does not reflect its natural game — Connor Beasley will need to decide early whether to fight for position or accept the rear rank.

races.paceDynamic: Why Not Me is the confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners over 1m3f at Ripon on Good ground, is set to control this race from the off at a sustainable, uncontested gallop. Time Thief will press or sit just off the pace in second, making this a two-horse dominant front group, while Masterly's unknown style leaves him an unpredictable element. Feelin' Free is a natural prominent type who cannot get that position here — with Why Not Me and Time Thief filling the front two berths, Feelin' Free will be forced to race out of role in midfield, blunting its effectiveness. This race shape — a single honest but measured pace-setter on flat Good ground over a staying trip — strongly favours hold-up types who can deliver a sustained finish off the steady tempo, with Peace Belle and any horse capable of travelling smoothly into contention in the final quarter-mile best positioned to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Why Not Me controls a comfortable gallop and the race is truly run at an honest but not pressured tempo, setting up a straight finishing contest.
scenarios.body: Why Not Me dictates from the front without being harassed, creating a moderately run race where those closest to the pace or with a powerful sustained finish hold the advantage; the final two furlongs at Ripon will sort out those with genuine class and stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Why Not Me sets an unexpectedly strong gallop that burns off chasers early and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Why Not Me, uncontested and fully relaxed through the early stages, saves enough energy to repel late challengers rounding the final bend; Time Thief, tracking closest, is the primary threat but may find the leader too well-rated to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Time Thief pushes Why Not Me along from early, lifting the gallop and ensuring the two front horses gallop rivals into submission.
scenarios.body: An elevated tempo suits horses already prominent and able to sustain it, with the race becoming a two-horse battle between Why Not Me and Time Thief from the two-furlong pole; hold-up horses Peace Belle and the displaced Feelin' Free find too much to do from off a fast pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overpower Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and hold-up runners conjure a sprint finish that sweeps past a tiring front group.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle, given a patient ride by Jason Hart, would be ideally positioned to pounce if the leaders have gone too hard earlier; however, this scenario is undermined by the genuinely steady nature of the likely pace and the fact that Feelin' Free — displaced to midfield — is not a natural hold-up horse and cannot be relied upon to execute that role cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Why Not Me's stamina for 1m3f is unproven — watch whether Oisin Murphy is able to keep a true rhythm or whether the horse idles and becomes vulnerable in the final two furlongs.

Feelin' Free has been redistributed to midfield but is a natural prominent type — watch the early stages to see if Connor Beasley elects to push forward regardless, which could disrupt the anticipated pace map entirely.

Masterly returns from 1,077 days off the track with just one career start — watch the market move in the final 30 minutes as any stable confidence will show price movements on a horse with so little public form to assess.

Time Thief's jockey David Egan will be key to positioning — if he sits a length behind Why Not Me rather than alongside, it signals confidence in the pace and that he is happy to let the race develop; any sign of pressure on the leader early shifts the scenario probabilities materially.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Ripon Champion Two Yrs Old Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Napa
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Kevin Philippart De Foy returning after 95 days off; all three career runs on good ground, beaten favourite last time at 5f, stepping up to 6f now which is an open question given a form string of 4-1-8.

runners_data.name: Pure Mint
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start, landing a good-ground 6f novice in convincing fashion; the class ceiling here at OR=120 makes her the headline act, and Harry Davies (Simon & Ed Crisford operation firing at 3/21 in 14 days) gives every reason to expect a bold show.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for the Easterbys, lightly weighted at OR=77 and racing just 12 days ago; one win from four starts (over 5f), now tackling 6f in a Listed race — the step in class and trip both require improvement.

runners_data.name: Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing a hood, trained in Ireland by Adrian Keatley (1/17 in 14 days); form figures of 2-3-1-8-5 show the win came over 6f on good but recent efforts have been patchy, and he faces strong competition for the lead here.

runners_data.name: Harry Knows
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a terrific six-race form record (2-4-2-2-1-3), winning over 6f good and placing four more times; PJ McDonald is an astute ally and the Ripon trip and surface are proven, making him a key player in any scenario where the pace is contested.

runners_data.name: Not My Type
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out a two-from-two speedster stepping up in grade sharply after back-to-back 5f wins on good; front-running style will be tested by Pure Mint and Co for supremacy, and the step to 6f and Listed level represents a significant leap.

runners_data.name: Rogue Jewel
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two 6f wins on good ground for Edward Bethell and Daniel Tudhope, one of the strongest jockey-trainer combinations in the north; a prominent style suits the anticipated tempo, and identical course-distance-going form makes him a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Silent Beauty
runners_data.note: Second Philippart De Foy runner, off 73 days since finishing unplaced at Chester on good-to-firm after a 6f Soft win; the gelding's record at the preferred distance is mixed and a lack of recent racecourse action in a hot field is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Mint, Clash Of Hearts, Napa, and Not My Type all carry front-running profiles, guaranteeing a contested, high-tempo gallop from the break over Ripon's straight six — this is not a race where any leader gets a soft lead. Pure Mint (OR=120) is the class standout and will likely dictate if she gets her head in front, but Clash Of Hearts and Napa will push hard for position in the early stages, creating genuine pace pressure from the outset. Harry Knows and Rogue Jewel — both prominent-to-handy types — will be poised just behind the scrap, positioned to capitalise if the pace burns out the leaders. With four horses fighting for the front and none likely to yield, this race shape strongly favours the hold-up and prominent runners who can sit off the pace and launch a sustained finish, particularly those with proven stamina for a hot-run six furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fast Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the multi-runner pace duel burns out the front-runners in the final furlong, leaving energy for the prominent-to-handy types to reel them in.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop from Pure Mint, Clash Of Hearts, and Napa sets a frantic tempo that tests all the leaders' reserves, cracking them late; Harry Knows and Rogue Jewel, sitting just off the early frenzy, are ideally placed to absorb and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pure Mint Dominates Class
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Mint's superior class (OR=120) allows her to control the pace on her own terms and quicken clear despite the early competition.
scenarios.body: Pure Mint's rating is 24lb clear of Clash Of Hearts and effectively a different league from most of the field; Harry Davies, a polished jockey, can settle her into the lead and use her class to grind rivals into submission through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not ruinous, allowing the prominent types to track the leaders comfortably and overhaul them in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Harry Knows (six previous runs, excellent form record of 1-2-2-2-4-3, thrives in prominent role on good ground) and Rogue Jewel (unbeaten in two on good, 6f course form) are both ideally suited to track and pick off tiring pace horses late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace surprisingly moderates — perhaps Clash Of Hearts or Napa back off early — giving one leader a more comfortable time of it.
scenarios.body: A reduced pace contest could see a single front-runner produce a longer, sustained gallop that the hold-up horses fail to reel in before the line; Not My Type (two wins from two, lightly raced, improving) could also emerge as an unlikely leader if rivals check.

watchPoints.text: Pure Mint's rivals — particularly Clash Of Hearts and Napa — will challenge her for the early lead hard; watch the first two furlongs to see whether she gets clear or is dragged into a war that saps her stamina.

Harry Knows has posted four placings from six runs but is yet to win a race at this level — watch whether PJ McDonald rides him conservatively off the pace or commits earlier than usual given the likely strong gallop.

Rogue Jewel's two wins have both been easy affairs in novice company; a significant step up to Listed level against horses rated 20-34lb above him means the acid test comes in the final furlong when class tells.

Not My Type's jump from 5f to 6f and from maiden/novice level to Listed in one step is the steepest profile ask in the race — watch how Tom Marquand positions her early, as covering too much ground in a pace war could compromise her finishing effort.

Silent Beauty (73 days off) and Bear Lee (OR=77 in a Listed) are the two runners most likely to be quickly swamped by the pace — monitor their market moves at the off, as drifting odds would confirm market intelligence about their readiness or suitability.

races.name: Ripon Rowels Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: English Oak
runners_data.note: Strong course record at the mile trip on Good ground with two wins and four places from similar conditions over 7f–8f; hold-up style suits a late-running scenario but needs genuine pace to burn ahead, which Milteye alone may not supply.|

runners_data.name: Thunder Roar
runners_data.note: 87 days off the track is a concern, and its sole Good-ground result at this trip was a second in 2019 — the sim-going record (2/15) is the weakest in the field; hold-up style means it needs pace and gaps that may not materialise.|

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a consistent finishing position in the 7th-to-9th range in recent starts, flagged as fading in the finish; David O'Meara's 14-day strike rate is solid but this horse's late fade pattern on Good ground over 8f is a real negative.|

runners_data.name: Mr Professor
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride on a hold-up type whose Good-ground record at this trip is sparse (3/15 sim-going, no wins or places); its best form has come on Soft or Standard, and it has not threatened from behind at this distance on Good.|

runners_data.name: Racingbreaks Ryder
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking is the headline; Charles Hills's 2/21 in 14 days reflects a horse being placed carefully, and back-to-back wins on Standard suggest Ryder is in form — the concern is that its best results came on artificial, and Good turf is unproven with just one similar-going run.|

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: Consistent placer whose natural trailing style — four of its last five runs finishing in the frame from hold-up — has been pushed to midfield by field congestion; racing out of its ideal position tempers its chance, though its trainer O'Meara runs two in this race and Tudhope is an astute judge of how to extricate a run.|

runners_data.name: Milteye
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner; Harriet Bethell sends it out with an apprentice claiming 5lb which eases the weight burden, and it has won from the front at this trip on Soft — Good ground and a flat course like Ripon suit its style but it must be respected as the pace-setter rather than a winner on current form.|

runners_data.name: Firefall
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's unexposed three-year-old with a win over 10f on Standard and a placed effort at 8f on Good; a 68-day break is worth monitoring but the Bethell yard are in form (T14: 4/27) and the horse has the profile of one running below its ceiling — an each-way profile in a shape where prominent runners do the pressing.|

runners_data.name: Majestic Dane
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's three-year-old with just two career starts (second and first) both on Standard at 7f — this is a significant step up into unknowns: Good turf, 8f, a handicap, and 193 days off; Burke's powerful 14-day record (9/44) maintains relevance but the unknowns stack up against confident assessment.|

races.paceDynamic: Milteye is the lone confirmed front-runner and, ridden by apprentice Ethan Tindall, is likely to be sent straight to the front from the off, setting a controlled and sustainable pace over this flat mile at Ripon on Good ground. The prominent group is congested — Mirsky, Racingbreaks Ryder, Firefall, and Majestic Dane all want to race close to the pace, meaning there will be immediate competition for positions two through five, creating potential traffic friction and shuffling between the two- and three-furlong markers. That prominent battle may compress the field as they round for home, compacting gaps and squeezing out hold-up runners who need daylight late. This race shape strongly favours horses that can secure a clean prominent pitch just behind Milteye and produce a sustained run into the straight — pure hold-up horses face a congested inside and a test of their ability to find a gap. The field carries more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Spoken Truth, a genuine hold-up operator, has been redistributed to midfield and is unlikely to secure its natural trailing position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Milteye Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Milteye sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent quartet settle cleanly behind.
scenarios.body: Milteye dictates a fair tempo from the front, and the best-placed prominent horse — one that tracked without getting embroiled in early jostling — picks them off in the final furlong on the flat Ripon straight; Good ground rewards a smooth, sustained effort rather than an explosive late burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Run Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Milteye's pace is slow enough that a prominent horse breezes alongside early and neither is seriously challenged until late.
scenarios.body: A sub-group of two sets sail in front, turning a competitive handicap into a pacemaker duel; the winner is whichever of that pair has the superior finishing kick and is ridden more conservatively in the first half.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominent traffic bunches tightly and creates a gap on the outside for a horse making ground from off the pace.
scenarios.body: English Oak, racing off a proper hold-up pitch, benefits if the pace is genuinely honest and the field spreads wide; its Good-ground course form suits but it needs the front end to burn each other out, which a lone and controlled Milteye makes less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos in the Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types fail to settle their positions quickly and the race turns scrappy with repeated checking and rank riding.
scenarios.body: Traffic incidents two to three out disrupt the rhythm of the fancied prominent runners, handing an advantage to any horse that is either clear at the front or entirely unaffected at the rear; a runner that threads a clean passage from midfield profits most.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Mirsky, Racingbreaks Ryder, Firefall, and Majestic Dane all want the same early positions; watch the first two furlongs for shuffling, bumping, or one of these runners being checked sharply, which could compromise their entire race.|

Milteye's apprentice rider Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) has no pressure on the front end but may either dawdle or allow the pace to be unrealistically slow — if the tempo is false, prominent rivals will be sent alongside earlier than expected, disrupting Milteye's rhythm.|

Spoken Truth is operating out of its natural hold-up position; if Tudhope is forced to push forward from midfield to find daylight, the horse burns energy earlier than ideal and its style-fit discount becomes a real performance drag.|

English Oak's trainer Hamad Al Jehani has 2 wins from 15 runners in 14 days — a modest but live rate; Harry Vigors claims 5lb on a horse with a genuine Good-ground mile record, and its finishing position will depend almost entirely on whether genuine pace develops in front of it.|

Majestic Dane returns after 193 days — K. R. Burke freshens horses effectively but a first run on turf, over a new trip, against older handicappers is a significant ask; monitor in-running for signs of greenness or tiring after three furlongs.|

races.name: Book Online At Ripon-races.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Gemma Tutty with a fine record at 5f on Good (12 qualifications, 3 wins, 6 places); ran second here 16 days ago and Connor Beasley knows this track, so a clear late run is the requirement.|

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has been placed in four of her last five on Good going and races just five days after her last run, suggesting freshness is not a concern; a natural prominent type who must secure a clear position early given the crowded second rank.|

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old has good course-distance form (2 wins, 7 places in similar conditions) and James Sullivan rides; needs to overcome the prominent-position congestion early, but has the consistency at this trip to reward if she gets a clean run.|

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's eight-year-old has won twice at 5f on Good and, crucially, won five days ago — quick back-to-back raider angle worth noting; Jason Hart rides and the horse genuinely wants to be prominent, putting him right in the thick of the early positional battle.|

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Three wins from eleven at 5f on Good is a solid record and Oisin Murphy brings top-level tactical intelligence; Paul Midgley trains him alongside Glory Fighter, and as a genuine hold-up type he needs the pace to be strong enough to deliver a meaningful closing run.|

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and four-time 5f Good winner from her last five starts; Oliver Carmichael takes the 7lb claimer's allowance and she carries 137lbs, but uncontested pace control at Ripon is a significant edge.|

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran who has shown he can win at 5f on Good but whose recent form (6th, 6th, 15th) is discouraging; Paul Midgley's second string, held up naturally, and will need a flawless late run that his current form line does not strongly advertise.|

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old is natural prominent ground but must compete for a limited number of those positions; ran 2nd at this trip on Good in his penultimate run and at 4 is the youngest in the field, though recent form (7th latest) shows inconsistency.|

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: In fine form with two recent wins including one at 5f on Good, but Martin Keighley's six-year-old is a natural prominent type that the congested race shape has displaced into midfield; Harry Vigors (5lb) claims, but racing out of its preferred position tempers the expected impact of that good recent form.|

races.paceDynamic: Thornaby Pearl is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse natural to the lead, she can dictate an honest but uncontested gallop from stall to line over this sharp 5f at Ripon. However, the prominent berths are heavily contested — Canaria Queen, Betweenthesticks, Our Absent Friends, and Marajito all want to race close to the pace, creating a congested pack behind the leader that raises traffic and interference risk between the 2f and 3f poles. Happier is a natural prominent type redistibuted to midfield because the field holds more front-running and prominent horses than can realistically all find their natural position; of the genuine prominent runners, Our Absent Friends and Canaria Queen — both proven in this grade at 5f on Good — are best-placed to claim those slots. With one controlled pace-setter and a high volume of horses chasing her at close quarters, this race shape most favours horses that can race prominently without burning excess energy in the early scramble, and genuine hold-up closers who find a clear lane late on the quick Ripon straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thornaby Pearl Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl leads unopposed and sets a sustainable rhythm that rewards those tracking cleanly.
scenarios.body: Thornaby Pearl has won three of her last five at 5f on Good and with no rival prepared to seriously contest her lead, she can control the tempo and prove very hard to peg back; horses like Our Absent Friends and Canaria Queen who settle just off her shoulder in clear air are ideally positioned to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the chasing group races hard to Thornaby Pearl's quarters early, increasing pace and leaving her vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A hotter-than-expected early pace caused by the scramble for prominent spots blunts Thornaby Pearl's stamina, bringing the race back to those who tracked slightly further back; Canaria Queen and Betweenthesticks, both multiple placed at this trip on Good, are positioned to profit as the leader ties.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominent battle creates a truly strong gallop that exposes the field, gifting the hold-up horses a clear finishing run.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England has won twice at 5f on Good and Mark's Choice ran second at this course recently; both are genuine hold-up types who benefit if the pace is hot enough to create a gap-finding opportunity through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion between 2f-3f out causes significant interference that scrambles the natural race order entirely.
scenarios.body: With four horses competing for two or three prominent positions, bumping and checking is a real possibility that could unluckily stop a well-placed runner; in this scenario any horse finding a clear passage — regardless of position — holds an advantage, with Marajito or Rock Of England potentially the beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Canaria Queen, Betweenthesticks, Our Absent Friends, and Marajito all want the same prominent positions — watch for bumping and crowding in the first 2f as they compete for ground behind Thornaby Pearl.

Thornaby Pearl's control of tempo is the race's single biggest variable — if she is pressured into an unsustainably fast early quarter-mile by the chasing pack, the entire race shape inverts and the hold-up horses become live players.

Happier, displaced from her natural prominent position, may get a rough passage racing out of role through midfield with Harry Vigors (5lb) having limited room for manoeuvre — watch for a run that flatters only in hindsight.

Rock Of England and Mark's Choice, both genuine hold-up types, require a strong pace and a clear lane through the final furlong — Ripon's straight finish suits late runners, but they are at the mercy of what the front groups create.

Our Absent Friends runs just five days after her last start; a quick turnaround for an eight-year-old is worth monitoring in the paddock, as any sign of staleness could undermine what otherwise looks a strong positional claim.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old in excellent heart for Ruth Carr, placing in ten of fifteen recent outings on similar going; a natural prominent racer who gets her ideal position here and whose consistency over 1m on good makes the step up to 1m2f the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's five-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and has experience over both 10f and 12f on good ground; the good going suits and with no rivals willing to press, the concern is whether OR 49 form is strong enough to hold on late rather than getting the lead at all.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: David Allan takes the ride on Tim Easterby's nine-year-old, a genuine hold-up type with a record of finishing second in good-ground races; no wins from fifteen similar-going starts is a concern, but he plugs on honestly and the extra furlong may extract a little more.

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is an obvious booking for Gihan Arnolda's horse, but this is a natural deep hold-up operator whose profile loses some edge here — the map places him in midfield rather than at the back where he would naturally hunt, and his form does not include a win or place in nine attempts on comparable going.

runners_data.name: Top Gun Tina
runners_data.note: David Thompson's six-year-old has no wins or places from fifteen outings on good ground; her race record of four to six finishes repeatedly over 7f-8f on standard ground raises a combination of distance and going suitability doubts, and she is a horse the style-fit discount applies to meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old has a tidy record of placed efforts on good going and over 8f-9f trips, and the step up to 1m2f on a sound surface represents a reasonable test; holds up and needs something to run at, which is unlikely to be provided generously today.

runners_data.name: Due To Shine
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's three-year-old is a hold-up type in a field with too many closers for them all to come from the rear; a 0-from-eight record on this sort of going and a recent poor finish at 12f on good ground make the case for selection thin regardless of positioning complications.

runners_data.name: Princess Coco
runners_data.note: The fades-in-finish flag is a clear concern for Simon Whitaker's filly, who has posted a run of 0, 9, 7, 12, 11 in her last five — a genuine hold-up operator placed in midfield on the map, but form this poor and an official rating of 43 make her extremely difficult to support in any shape.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides the Michael & David Easterby three-year-old who is the most lively form horse in the field — a winner at 8f on good ground recently and placed three times in her last five; raced off just 6 days ago (visor noted) and the 1m2f trip may be the stretching factor, but her good-ground form is genuinely the strongest here.

runners_data.name: Twin And Tonic
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old has only three career runs, finishing 4th, 9th, and 11th, and carries a fades-in-finish flag on top of being a hold-up type displaced to midfield; very limited evidence, but nothing in the form suggests she can be competitive at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Ripon contest and should slot comfortably into the lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on good ground without any realistic rival prepared to press hard from the front. Copper And Five is the only other horse with a genuine prominent style and will likely track Inspiring Speeches in second, giving the race a relatively strung-out, steady-tempo complexion from the first furlong. The remainder of the field — including Rogers Dream, Top Gun Tina, Due To Shine, Princess Coco, and Twin And Tonic — are natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the true closers will be bunched in a group behind a modest pace, waiting for something to happen that may never fully materialise. This race shape strongly favours the horse who can lead or track close to a gentle gallop and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than those relying on a late surge from deep; Inspiring Speeches dictating and Copper And Five pressing on the pace are the profiles best suited to how this race will be run. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically come from the back against a single uncontested front-runner, and Inspiring Speeches is most likely to secure the front rail, with Copper And Five the one genuinely able to take the position directly behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a comfortable, controlled tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Inspiring Speeches controls every yard of the race on good ground, and the moderate pace means stamina reserves are preserved for a sustained run rather than a sprint finish; a horse able to travel prominently and outstay rivals into the Ripon straight wins this. Copper And Five, positioned just off the shoulder, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader ties up, while Trucial Pearl — showing recent good form over this trip on good ground — can make ground from midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches sets a crawl and Copper And Five or a prominent tracker moves past decisively turning for home.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace collapses into a dash for home in the final two furlongs, heavily favouring horses who have tracked the speed and can quicken; Copper And Five's consistent placed form on good ground and prominent style make her the chief beneficiary. Trucial Pearl, who has won on good ground over shorter and is in good recent form, also has the profile to pick off a fading leader from a handy position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong enough to string out the field and allow genuine closers to close late.
scenarios.body: Volenti has repeatedly posted placed efforts chasing home leaders over this sort of trip and ground, and a slightly stronger-than-expected tempo would bring him into contention in the closing stages. Little Ted and Rogers Dream have hold-up credentials and could fill the frame, though Rogers Dream's redistribution from rear to midfield means its natural closing run may be partially compromised by a wider-than-ideal pitch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If no horse settles properly, the pace implodes, and the field bunches turning in.
scenarios.body: With several horses uncomfortable out of their natural positions and a lone genuine front-runner who may be vulnerable if the race becomes messy, a chaotic finish cannot be ruled out entirely. In such conditions, a horse with tactical versatility and good recent form like Trucial Pearl — who has finished first or placed in three of its last four — could prove adaptable enough to profit from confusion.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches (front-runner) — watch whether Ethan Tindall allows her to stride on comfortably or is pressured into going too fast too soon, because the entire race shape hinges on her controlling the tempo from the front.

Copper And Five — James Sullivan must secure a prominent pitch immediately from the gate; if she is shuffled back into the pack behind the redistributed hold-up horses she loses her positional edge and her chance narrows sharply.

Trucial Pearl — six days between runs plus the visor retained and the step to 1m2f are all worth monitoring in the betting; she has the best recent form, but if the trip stretches her stamina she may fade despite tracking the pace well enough early.

Rogers Dream and Oisin Murphy — despite the high-profile jockey booking, this horse's natural running style is compromised by the race shape; watch for Murphy to try an uncharacteristically forward move to counteract the position disadvantage, which could be telling about how connections view the horse's prospects.

Volenti — three consecutive placed efforts on good ground suggest quiet consistency; if the early pace is stronger than expected and the field strings out, he is the hold-up type with the clearest evidence of sustaining a challenge at the business end.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Classified Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: The lone natural front-runner here, and David Egan can exploit that uncontested lead role fully; nine-year-old with an OR=49 win last time out seven furlongs ago on Good, steps up to 1m2f which is a query but his pace control is the key asset.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in form at 4/71 in 14 days and this five-year-old wears a tongue-piece; she's a genuine hold-up horse with a Good-ground placing at 8f on similar terrain, though her recent form string (969064) demands a significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Golden Samba
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this four-year-old who has useful form over staying trips (14f-17f) but drops back to 1m2f here; a true hold-up horse whose natural style places her at the rear, so she arrives in midfield on the map but will likely settle towards the back of the field in running.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a horse whose recent history shows three Good-ground placings over 10f — directly relevant experience; a genuine hold-up type who should get a favourable position tracking the midfield bunch and has the form profile to sustain a challenge.

runners_data.name: Tiberio Force
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's seven-year-old wears blinkers and has been consistent at 10f on Good recently (six consecutive runs at that distance), though finishing positions of 6-9 are uninspiring; pushed into a midfield slot but his true preference is to race held up, and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: David Thompson's eight-year-old carries a headgear change (p) and has a very poor recent record (800988) with no Good-ground placing in 15 attempts on that surface; a true closer forced into a busier midfield position, making an already difficult task harder.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's three-year-old is lightly weighted at 128lbs and has some experience over 10f on Good (placed once), but all five recent runs ended in the back half of the field; a natural hold-up horse who needs much more than this form suggests.

runners_data.name: Captain Bruce
runners_data.note: Andrew Crook's three-year-old has a specific finishing fade flag and has been beaten out of sight on Good ground repeatedly (5/13 sim-going, 0 wins, 0 places); the redistribution into midfield compounds an already bleak profile, and 63 days off is a further query.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley sends this three-year-old up from OR=32 — the lowest-rated runner in the field — wearing a hood; limited form over 8f on Tapeta and Fibresand, and Good-ground turf form is sparse at just 2/4 attempts; his true hold-up style means he arrives at the rear naturally but improvement is needed throughout.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners the highest-rated three-year-old (OR=50) for in-form David O'Meara (3/39 in 14 days); nine of his ten runs have come on Good ground with three placings, and the step to 1m2f from 8f looks a logical progression — the strongest profile among the hold-up horses.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Ripon contest and, with no other natural pace-pusher to challenge, will stride to the front from the outset and control a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. The majority of the field are genuine hold-up types — Ten Sixty Six, Quirke On Parole, Evelyn's Phoenix and others — who will settle in behind and wait for their moment entering the straight. This field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Balance Of Trade, Captain Bruce, Tiberio Force, Golden Samba, Wheres The Crumpet and Retro Rocket are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots, meaning they are likely to race in a compressed bunch behind Back From Dubai rather than settling as true closers. With a single uncontested front-runner setting a controlled pace over a trip where stamina is tested, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel comfortably in midfield and produce a sustained late challenge through the final two furlongs — horses who are genuinely comfortable waiting and finishing are at the maximum advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Pacer Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai dictates an uncontested, controlled gallop and the pursuing hold-up pack fails to close the gap efficiently through the Ripon straight.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai sets his own fractions with zero pressure, conserving energy through the middle stages, and his rider David Egan can time the escalation of pace perfectly entering the final quarter-mile; on Good ground at this OR=49 level, a well-rated nine-year-old in his preferred role has every chance of lasting home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses — particularly those with genuine form at this trip on Good ground — travel powerfully in the bunch and collectively overwhelm Back From Dubai in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Ten Sixty Six (OR=50, sim-going 9/10, handled by Daniel Tudhope for David O'Meara who has three winners in 14 days) and Quirke On Parole (three Good-ground placings at 10f in recent history) are best placed to deliver a sustained challenge; the compressed midfield bunch gives them cover and a clean run if the pace unravels.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the large cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — all racing closer than their natural style — create interference and traffic in the straight, opening a gap for the truest closers to weave through late.
scenarios.body: Evelyn's Phoenix (headgear: tp, Tim Easterby's yard 4/71 in 14 days, solid Good-ground record) and Quirke On Parole are among the most genuine hold-up horses in the field and benefit if chaos in the midfield bunch leaves them with clear daylight late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai overcooks the early fractions or fades dramatically in the straight, turning this into a cavalry charge from the compressed pack.
scenarios.body: An unlikely shape given the absence of any pace pressure forcing Back From Dubai's hand, but if it occurs the hold-up horses with the highest OR ratings and best recent form — Ten Sixty Six and Quirke On Parole — are best positioned to capitalise on a vacated lead.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai (David Egan) dictates every fraction unchallenged — watch whether Egan conserves energy through the first mile or allows the pace to drift dangerously slow, as that timing decision shapes the entire race.

Ten Sixty Six has the highest OR among the three-year-olds and Tudhope will need to find a clear run through the compressed midfield cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — traffic in the straight is a real risk for this profile.

The six redistributed hold-up horses (Balance Of Trade, Captain Bruce, Tiberio Force, Golden Samba, Wheres The Crumpet, Retro Rocket) are all likely to race closer than their natural style dictates, creating a densely packed midfield that could cause significant interference entering the final bend.

Quirke On Parole's three Good-ground placings over 10f give him the most directly relevant course-and-distance profile among the hold-up group — Jason Hart's positioning from the wide draw will be worth monitoring in the early stages.

Evelyn's Phoenix (tongue-piece, Easterby yard in form) has the widest recent going spread of the field — watch whether she travels comfortably in the first half-mile, as her finishing effort on Good has historically come only when she's settled early.

races.name: Aja Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 7-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who needs things to fall right late on; 21 days since last run is a workable freshness window, good ground is fine, but the 1m3f trip is longer than its best recent efforts at 10f and the closing run may arrive too late in an honest-paced race.

runners_data.name: Jam Lass
runners_data.note: 133 days off the track is a significant concern for Peter Niven's mare, and the step back to good ground after stalls form is uncertain; a confirmed hold-up style means she needs a thorough pace to close into, and the layoff makes it hard to trust her to produce a peak effort here.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's 4-year-old has shown ability at trips around 11-14f and wears headgear (p), suggesting an attempt to sharpen concentration; zero wins on good ground from three tries is a mild worry, but the horse has placed twice recently and a hold-up style could work if the pace holds.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 5-year-old has two wins at 10f on good ground and returns quickly on just 9 days' rest; in truth a hold-up horse by nature, it has been placed in midfield here because the field's rear is oversubscribed — racing out of its natural deep position reduces its chance of delivering a winning performance.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has a strong 14-day record (4/71) and this prominent-travelling mare has won four times at 10f on good ground, making her one of the better pace-fit profiles in the race; the step to 1m3f is a question, but she has placed from a tracking position and headgear (p) is familiar.

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's 7-year-old landed a win at 12f on soft ground but has gone 0 from 8 on good going, which is a serious concern here; a hold-up horse by preference, it finds itself mapped to midfield because the rear is full — that positional compromise, combined with the poor good-ground record, makes this a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6-year-old is the key pace figure, with three wins and eight places from 12 good-ground runs showing genuine affinity for conditions; Miss Charli Parker takes a 5lb claim which partially offsets the weight, and this horse's record of placing or winning at 10-12f makes it the most likely to control proceedings from the front.

runners_data.name: Three Yorkshiremen
runners_data.note: Jack Jones's 6-year-old has produced a dismal form string of 89957 with zero wins or places on either standard or good going, and 41 days off the track adds uncertainty; a prominent style means the horse will at least be involved in the early stages, but there is little evidence to suggest it can hold that position to the line at this trip.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 4-year-old has placed five times without winning on good ground and shaped well at 8f earlier in the season; its natural inclination is to come from the back, but with several hold-up types vying for the same ground late, it is mapped to midfield — the short-to-good trip may suit better than longer STA outings suggest.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's 5-year-old runs just 4 days after its last start, which is a fitness point worth noting but could also indicate it is in a productive spell; five places at 9-12f on good ground without a win suggest it is better suited to making the pace than winning the race, and its role here is likely to test Star Start rather than to win outright.

races.paceDynamic: Star Start and On The Bubble are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 1m3f trip at Ripon, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a false, slow-burn pace. With both horses pressing each other through the first half of the race on good ground, the tempo should be honest enough to stretch the field and expose those who cannot travel, making it a test of stamina and tactical positioning rather than a sprint finish. The field contains more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate — Woodleigh, Cougar, and Glitter Code are all natural hold-up horses redistributed toward midfield on the map because they are unlikely to secure their preferred deep position in this shape. This contested pace scenario on a flat, fair track on good ground most favours prominent or midfield runners with proven stamina at the trip, who can track the battle without being embroiled in it and pick up the pieces when the front two inevitably tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Burn Out
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start and On The Bubble press each other into a truly honest gallop and drain each other's reserves before the home turn.
scenarios.body: The pace duel sets a solid tempo that brings the finish well within reach of the closers tracking in midfield, and those who have settled a length or two off the early leaders find themselves with a decisive advantage entering the straight. Prominent types who have been switched off behind the duel and have the stamina for 1m3f on good ground are ideally placed to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Frontrunner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If On The Bubble fades or is restrained early, leaving Star Start to find a comfortable solo lead at a measured pace.
scenarios.body: Star Start, who has strong good-going form and has been placed or won at this trip on multiple recent occasions, settles into her own rhythm and makes it a test of class rather than stamina attrition. Without a true battle up front, the pace becomes moderate enough that prominent horses get a soft lead to follow but find it harder to quicken past a fresh, uncontested pace-setter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front two go hard enough to create significant stopping ground and the true back-markers find clear daylight late.
scenarios.body: Spirit Catcher and Jam Lass are the genuine hold-up horses in this field with some good-going form and the experience to close from off the pace, but both carry the burden of needing everything to go right positionally in a race where midfield congestion is likely. This scenario is tempered by the fact that Woodleigh, Cougar, and Glitter Code — natural hold-up types themselves — are crowding the rear and limiting the space for a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If the duel between Star Start and On The Bubble dies early and the field bunches into a falsely run affair.
scenarios.body: A messy, slow-tempo race over 1m3f on good ground dissolves into a sprint finish in the straight, which suits no one's profile particularly well given the lack of a proven short-range finisher in the field. Three Yorkshiremen, who has struggled for form but holds a prominent position and may benefit from chaos, or It's Only Fun with its front-foot headgear are the only horses with any realistic claim if this shape materialises.

watchPoints.text: Star Start and On The Bubble are on a collision course for the lead — watch how aggressively Miss Charli Parker and Miss Emma J Brown ride the first two furlongs, as the intensity of that duel will determine whether this is a true-run 1m3f or a stop-start affair.

Jam Lass returns from 133 days off for Peter Niven; watch her in the pre-race paddock and early on for any sign of ring-rustiness, as a hold-up horse needing a big finish is the last profile to forgive a layoff.

Woodleigh, Cougar, and Glitter Code — all natural hold-up horses — will be competing for the same late ground; watch for traffic trouble in the straight if all three attempt to find a run simultaneously from similar positions.

Kitsune Power's jockey Miss Amy Collier will need to decide early whether to track the front two or drop in behind them; if she follows Star Start too closely, she risks being caught up in the pace duel rather than benefiting from it.

On The Bubble's 4-day turnaround means its jumping-off tactics may be dictated by how fresh it feels rather than race strategy — watch it in the stalls and first furlong for any sign it is not fully committed to making the early running.
